rules.statement: A servitude of emphyteusis can be acquired by prescription under the Prescription Ordinance, even if it involves a payment of one-third of the produce.
rules.supporting_quote: 'I think, however, that the words "a possession unaccompanied by payment of rent or produce" are governed by the following words of the section: 'from which an acknowledgment of a right existing in another person would fairly and naturally be inferred' In the present case I consider that apart from the deed of 1836, which is inadmissible in evidence, it is quite obvious, and has been uncontested throughout the case, that the defendants and their predecessors have throughout and for very many years claimed to hold this land in perpetuity at a rent charge under some deed executed by Gallage Hendrick, and therefore that their claim to this servitude has been adverse to the plaintiffs and their predecessors; and the payment of one-third share of the proceeds of the land is not, under the circumstances, a payment from which an acknowledgment of a right existing in the plaintiffs and their predecessors in title to the land unburdened with the servitude, would fairly or reasonably be inferred.'
rules.statute_citation_verbatim: 'The expression 'immovable property' shall be taken to include an shares and interest in such property, and all rights, easements, and servitudes thereunto belonging or appertaining.' Section 2 of the Prescription Ordinance, 1871.
